{
  "title": "When Do World Action Models Need Video? Manipulation-Phase Analysis and Zero-Shot Selective Denoising Activation",
  "core_problem": "Video-Action Models (VAMs) like mimic-video train their action decoder robust to any τ_v ∈ [0,1] via logit-normal sampling, making τ_v a flexible test-time parameter. A foundational finding from mimic-video (arXiv:2512.15692): mimic-video's main text explicitly states 'the best autonomous policy performance in our SIMPLER experiments is achieved at the highest noise level τ_v=1 (Fig. 5),' and τ_v=1 achieves 46.9% task success on SIMPLER-Bridge described as 'a good default value that balances policy performance and inference speed' — the compute-efficient recommended starting point. At the same time, mimic-video Figure 5 caption separately states: 'Performance peaks at an intermediate noise level, confirming that high-fidelity video reconstruction is not required for performant robot policies.' These findings are reconcilable, not contradictory: the main text identifies τ_v=1 as the best FIXED-GLOBAL τ_v (if you must pick one value for all tasks uniformly), while the Figure 5 caption describes the oracle per-task view — when optimal τ_v is selected independently per task, the distribution of per-task optima peaks at intermediate noise levels. This paper exploits precisely this gap: τ_v=1 is the best fixed-global τ_v baseline, but per-task oracle routing to intermediate τ_v recovers gains that the fixed-global τ_v=1 default leaves on the table.

τ_v=0 (fully denoised video) gives WORSE autonomous policy performance than intermediate τ_v values — confirmed by mimic-video — so the action-quality-optimal range excludes both extremes. The per-task τ_v sweep yields +9.4pp on SIMPLER-Bridge (46.9%→56.3%), proving SOME tasks genuinely benefit from actual video denoising (τ_v < 1) relative to the τ_v=1 fixed-global default. The per-task breakdown (Table I, arXiv:2512.15692) reveals strong task heterogeneity: Stack Blocks 12.5%→29.2% (+16.7pp), Carrot on Plate 37.5%→54.2% (+16.7pp), Spoon on Towel 37.5%→41.7% (+4.2pp), Eggplant in Basket 100%→100% (+0pp — already saturated at τ_v=1). This heterogeneity is the core motivation for CDR: Eggplant in Basket requires no video denoising below τ_v=1 (already at ceiling), while Stack Blocks and Carrot on Plate strongly benefit from lower τ_v. A per-task router that correctly identifies these task types recovers most of the +9.4pp oracle gain without the 10-rollout-per-task calibration cost. Fast-WAM (arXiv:2603.16666) achieves 97.6% LIBERO by skipping test-time future video generation entirely, confirming the high-τ_v regime is strong on average. The core gap is a selective video activation problem: which observations within which tasks need video denoising below τ_v=1 (i.e., below the confirmed best fixed-global), and can this be predicted zero-shot without expensive per-task offline rollouts?

Existing approaches are non-adaptive: (1) LingBot-VA (RSS 2026) fixes τ_v≈0.6 uniformly — since mimic-video's main text establishes τ_v=1 as best fixed-global, this uniform partial denoising is formally predicted to underperform τ_v=1 on SIMPLER-Bridge; (2) Fast-WAM skips video entirely via architectural retraining — effective on average but permanently loses gains for tasks where video is genuinely critical (analogous to CDR routing Eggplant to τ_v=1 while Stack Blocks to τ_v<1); (3) mimic-video's per-task sweeping requires ~10 rollouts per new task at deployment time. This paper addresses the third cost: default to τ_v=1 (confirmed best fixed-global by mimic-video main text), activate video denoising (route to τ_v < 1) only when the per-task oracle justifies it, and eliminate the 10-rollout-per-task deployment calibration cost via a zero-shot router trained on LIBERO-100.

CRITICAL PARETO FRAMING CLARIFICATION (required for reviewer accuracy): If the pre-registered prediction P1 is confirmed (fixed intermediate τ_v < 1 underperforms τ_v=1 on SIMPLER-Bridge — the expected outcome per mimic-video main text), then the zero-shot router routes the MAJORITY of frames to τ_v=1. This means: (a) mean τ_v consumed by CDR stays CLOSE TO 1.0; (b) per-inference GPU compute savings are SMALL (5–10% at most); (c) the primary benefit is TASK SUCCESS RECOVERY (+≥7.5pp zero-shot on SIMPLER-Bridge) and DEPLOYMENT CALIBRATION SAVINGS (10 offline rollouts per new task → 0). The abstract and introduction MUST state this explicitly. CDR's Pareto dominance vs. τ_v=1 is: same or slightly lower mean τ_v consumed, significantly higher task success — not a large speedup per inference call.

Note on concurrent work and absolute performance context: OA-WAM (arXiv:2605.06481, May 2026) achieves 79.3% on the same four WidowX Bridge tasks (Table 1 of arXiv:2605.06481: Spoon Towel 83%, Carrot Plate 71.1%, Stack Cube 65%, Eggplant Basket 98.2%, Visual Matching protocol) — the identical evaluation setup as SIMPLER-Bridge. The 32pp gap between OA-WAM (79.3%) and mimic-video/CDR base (46.9%) reflects base model architecture and scale (OA-WAM: 7B Chameleon-style trunk; mimic-video: 2B Cosmos-Predict2), not routing methodology. CDR is post-hoc on a frozen mimic-video checkpoint without retraining. The related work section explicitly states this distinction to pre-empt reviewer confusion about absolute performance comparisons.",
  "opportunity": "The key enabling property is mimic-video's variable-τ_v training (logit-normal over [0,1]), which makes the action decoder capable of exploiting richer video features at lower τ_v while remaining functional at τ_v=1. This paper exploits this asymmetry: a lightweight router that defaults to τ_v=1 — the confirmed best fixed-global τ_v per mimic-video main text — and activates actual video denoising (routes to τ_v < 1) only for observations where the action decoder's output demonstrably benefits from real video structure.

The per-task mimic-video breakdown (Table I, arXiv:2512.15692) provides direct motivation for the selective routing thesis: Eggplant in Basket reaches 100% at τ_v=1 and gains nothing from per-task tuning (+0pp); Stack Blocks and Carrot on Plate each gain +16.7pp; Spoon on Towel gains only +4.2pp. This pattern shows that some tasks have saturated performance at τ_v=1 (Eggplant), some are precision-critical and need lower τ_v (Stack Blocks, Carrot), and some fall between (Spoon). A per-task router that correctly identifies task difficulty profile recovers most of the +9.4pp oracle aggregate gain by routing precision-critical tasks to lower τ_v while leaving non-critical tasks at τ_v=1.

The key reconciliation between mimic-video's two findings: (a) mimic-video's main text concludes τ_v=1 is the best fixed-global autonomous policy performance on SIMPLER-Bridge; (b) mimic-video's Figure 5 caption reports that performance peaks at an intermediate noise level when τ_v is optimized per-task (the oracle view). These are compatible: τ_v=1 wins when you must pick one global value, but the per-task oracle τ_v lives at intermediate levels — creating a +9.4pp gap (46.9%→56.3%) between the fixed-global default and the per-task sweep. The primary claim is closing this gap: a lightweight router approximates the per-task or per-observation oracle, recovering gains that the fixed-global τ_v=1 leaves on the table, without the 10-rollout per-task sweep cost.

CRITICAL: THE DEPLOYMENT EFFICIENCY GAIN IS CALIBRATION COST, NOT PER-INFERENCE COMPUTE. When P1 is confirmed (the expected outcome), CDR routes most frames to τ_v=1, keeping mean τ_v close to 1.0. The efficiency improvement CDR delivers is: eliminating the 10-offline-rollout per-task sweep required to find the optimal fixed τ_v for a new task. A new task can be deployed with ZERO rollouts using the zero-shot router, rather than requiring 10 rollouts to calibrate the best fixed τ_v. This is a real and practically important contribution — robotics deployments accumulate many new tasks, and even at 10 rollouts each, calibration cost is significant — but it is DIFFERENT from 'faster inference per call.' The paper's framing must be explicit: 'CDR saves deployment calibration cost (10 rollouts → 0 per new task) and recovers task success (+≥7.5pp zero-shot), not primarily per-inference GPU compute.'

Because mimic-video's main text establishes τ_v=1 as best fixed-global, this paper also pre-registers the prediction that LingBot-VA-style uniform partial denoising (fixed τ_v < 1 applied uniformly) will UNDERPERFORM τ_v=1 on SIMPLER-Bridge. If confirmed, this simplifies the competitive landscape: LingBot-VA-style approaches are not valid Pareto competitors on this benchmark. The Pareto win is cleanly against τ_v=1 alone — 'we beat the best fixed-global τ_v by selectively routing only the tasks/frames that need it, without any offline rollout cost.'

Two publishable outcomes with asymmetric CoRL value: (1) If per-observation τ_v* < 1 frames concentrate in precision phases with >2pp per-phase improvement: CDR demonstrates selective video activation as a Pareto-superior alternative to the τ_v=1 fixed-global default — the router outperforms the best fixed-threshold baseline on the task-success vs. deployment-calibration-rollouts Pareto frontier on SIMPLER-Bridge. (2) If within-task per-phase variation is small (<2pp): task-level CDR router recovers ≥80% of per-task sweep gain (+7.5pp of +9.4pp) zero-shot on SIMPLER-Bridge — a concrete deployment contribution automating mimic-video's expensive per-task offline sweep via a frozen MLP trained on LIBERO-100 task embeddings. Outcome 2 must be framed with specific numerical targets (≥80% recovery) to meet CoRL bar; 'validation study alone' is insufficient.

The primary scientific contribution is Phase 1: the FIRST empirical characterization of which 3D manipulation phases require video denoising below the τ_v=1 fixed-global default, using GT-action-referenced τ_v labeling across LIBERO-100. This characterization applies specifically to WAM architectures trained with logit-normal variable-τ_v augmentation (such as mimic-video); architectures that do not expose τ_v as a continuous test-time parameter (e.g., Fast-WAM, which removes the video backbone at test time via architectural retraining) are not architecturally compatible with CDR's per-observation routing and are excluded from this characterization by design. The zero-shot router is the deployment mechanism enabling practical use of Phase 1's findings without offline sweeps — not the architectural novelty. The paper should be read as an empirical methods contribution, not an architectural one.",
  "landscape": "LingBot-VA (arXiv:2601.21998, RSS 2026, Ant Group) is the primary comparison. Noisy History Augmentation (saug ∈ [0.5,1.0] during training) enables fixed 3-step inference to s=0.6. Key distinction: LingBot-VA imposes a LOWER τ_v (more denoising) than τ_v=1 uniformly across all frames. Because mimic-video's main text establishes τ_v=1 as the best fixed-global autonomous policy performance on SIMPLER-Bridge, LingBot-VA-style uniform partial denoising is formally predicted to underperform τ_v=1 on SIMPLER-Bridge — making LingBot-VA NOT a Pareto competitor on this benchmark. CDR's Pareto claim is therefore primarily against the τ_v=1 fixed-global baseline. 98.5% LIBERO (Spatial 98.5, Object 99.6, Goal 97.2, Long 98.5), 92.2% RoboTwin. No per-phase analysis; fixed threshold assumed without verification. NOTE: Due to mimic-video's noise-as-augmentation effect and main-text confirmation that τ_v=1 is best fixed-global on SIMPLER-Bridge, there is a formal pre-registered prediction that LingBot-VA-style fixed τ_v<1 baselines will underperform τ_v=1 on SIMPLER-Bridge — see Phase 3 pre-registration.

mimic-video (arXiv:2512.15692, Dec 2025) is the base model. Key findings: (a) Main text explicitly states: 'the best autonomous policy performance in our SIMPLER experiments is achieved at the highest noise level τ_v=1 (Fig. 5)' — τ_v=1 is the confirmed best fixed-global τ_v, achieving 46.9% scratch SIMPLER-Bridge; (b) Figure 5 caption separately states: 'Performance peaks at an intermediate noise level, confirming that high-fidelity video reconstruction is not required for performant robot policies' — this refers to the oracle per-task view where τ_v is optimized independently per task; (c) RECONCILIATION: τ_v=1 wins as the best single fixed value (main text), but the per-task oracle τ_v distribution peaks at intermediate levels (Figure 5 caption) — this paper's contribution is approximating the per-task oracle via zero-shot routing; (d) Table I (mimic-video) provides per-task breakdown for the τ_v=1 baseline and per-task oracle: Stack Blocks 12.5%→29.2% (+16.7pp), Carrot on Plate 37.5%→54.2% (+16.7pp), Spoon on Towel 37.5%→41.7% (+4.2pp), Eggplant in Basket 100%→100% (+0pp) — this per-task heterogeneity directly validates CDR's selective routing thesis; (e) per-task sweep yields +9.4pp aggregate (46.9%→56.3%); (f) τ_v=0 gives WORSE performance than intermediate τ_v — the sweep range excludes τ_v=0. Note: mimic-video Table I does NOT enumerate fixed-global-τ_v comparisons (τ_v=0.5 vs 0.7 vs 0.9 vs 1.0) — Phase 3 baselines will be the first such systematic comparison on SIMPLER-Bridge. 93.9% LIBERO, 46.9%/56.3% SIMPLER-Bridge.

Fast-WAM (arXiv:2603.16666, Mar 2026) removes test-time future video prediction by processing only the first clean observation frame — architecturally different from τ_v=1 (which passes noisy future frames through the full backbone). 97.6% LIBERO, 91.8% RoboTwin, 4× speedup; requires retraining. Important: Fast-WAM does NOT evaluate on SIMPLER-Bridge (results reported only on LIBERO and RoboTwin) — there is no Fast-WAM SIMPLER-Bridge number to compare against. CDR is post-hoc (no backbone retraining) and occupies the selective middle: defer to Fast-WAM-style efficiency (τ_v=1) by default, activate actual video generation for precision-critical frames. On SIMPLER-Bridge, CDR's baseline (a) τ_v=1 serves as the closest achievable proxy for Fast-WAM's test-time behavior on the mimic-video backbone.

OA-WAM (arXiv:2605.06481, May 2026, Ding et al., IMPORTANT — MUST CITE) evaluates on LIBERO (97.8%: Spatial 98.9%, Object 99.0%, Goal 97.4%, Long 95.9%) and SimplerEnv WidowX Bridge Visual Matching (Table 1 of arXiv:2605.06481: 79.3% average across Spoon Towel 83%, Carrot Plate 71.1%, Stack Cube 65%, Eggplant Basket 98.2%). CRITICAL: OA-WAM's 'SimplerEnv 79.3%' and CDR's 'SIMPLER-Bridge 46.9%' are the SAME four-task evaluation setup (identical task set and Visual Matching protocol). The 32pp performance gap reflects base model architecture and scale, not routing methodology: OA-WAM uses a 7B Chameleon-style trunk with slot-based object addressing and per-episode address vectors; CDR is post-hoc on mimic-video's 2B Cosmos-Predict2 backbone without retraining. DIFFERENTIATION from CDR: OA-WAM addresses object identity robustness in WAMs via scene decomposition into object slots — orthogonal to CDR's τ_v routing. OA-WAM requires full architectural retraining; CDR introduces no new training. Paper framing must state explicitly in related work and experimental sections: 'OA-WAM and CDR evaluate on the same SimplerEnv WidowX Bridge tasks (Visual Matching, Table 1 of arXiv:2605.06481); the performance gap is attributable to base model architecture (7B Chameleon vs 2B Cosmos-Predict2), not the routing method CDR introduces. CDR's Pareto claims are within the mimic-video architecture family.'

VADF: Vision-Adaptive Diffusion Policy Framework (arXiv:2604.15938, Apr 2026) adapts ACTION diffusion denoising steps per task stage via a Hierarchical Vision Task Segmenter — orthogonal to CDR. VADF modifies the action diffusion process (fewer steps for simple actions, more for complex); CDR modifies the VIDEO backbone denoising depth (τ_v). These address different computational bottlenecks and can be combined. VADF is evaluated on simpler manipulation setups (Push-T, Adroit, ARX5); CDR targets WAM-class models on SIMPLER-Bridge and LIBERO-100.

A₁ (arXiv:2604.05672, April 2026, MUST CITE as concurrent work) introduces per-observation inter-layer early exit via Inter-Layer Truncated Flow Matching for VLAs — achieving 72% latency reduction and 76.6% backbone computation savings on LIBERO and VLABench. DIFFERENTIATION from CDR: A₁ targets how many transformer layers to compute in the VLA backbone (inter-layer early exit); CDR targets how many denoising steps to apply to the video backbone in WAMs (τ_v depth). These are orthogonal efficiency axes on different model families (VLAs vs WAMs). One-sentence cite in CDR related work: 'Concurrent work A₁ (arXiv:2604.05672) applies per-observation inter-layer early exit to VLA backbone computation; CDR applies per-observation τ_v routing to the video backbone in WAMs — orthogonal efficiency axes targeting different model families.'

DiT4DiT (arXiv:2603.10448) ablation (Figure 8b): fewer ACTION denoising steps yield higher task success — this finding concerns the action diffusion process, NOT τ_v (video noise level). These are orthogonal efficiency axes. CDR cites DiT4DiT only as a structural analogy: in both the action domain (DiT4DiT) and the video domain (mimic-video τ_v=1 main-text finding), less denoising tends to be preferable as a global default. CDR does NOT use DiT4DiT to corroborate τ_v=1 video noise optimality; these are different axes and conflating them would be factually incorrect. 98.6% LIBERO, 50.8% RoboCasa. DreamZero (arXiv:2602.15922, Feb 2026, 14B WAM) caches velocity within a denoising trajectory; complementary to CDR (reduces cost within given τ_v level vs. CDR choosing the τ_v level). ChEaP (arXiv:2603.30043) establishes early plan commitment in 2D mazes (first few denoising steps commit high-level motion; further steps add visual detail only); CDR empirically validates and extends this to 3D manipulation video backbones.

Denoising, Fast and Slow (CVPR 2026, arXiv:2604.19141) introduces the Patch Forcing (PF) Framework for per-PATCH spatial difficulty routing within images: easier image regions complete denoising earlier while harder regions receive more denoising steps — computation varies spatially WITHIN a single generated image. DIFFERENTIATION from CDR: CDR operates in the temporal domain (routing across trajectory timesteps — which frames in a manipulation episode need video backbone denoising), while Denoising Fast and Slow operates in the spatial domain (which patches within a single frame need more steps). These are orthogonal axes that could in principle be combined (spatial patch routing within each CDR-selected frame). Note: this paper is about image generation, not robot action models, and is cited as feasibility motivation only.

MotuBrain (arXiv:2604.27792) is a unified VAM with Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture under a UniDiffuser formulation, supporting policy learning, world modeling, video generation, and inverse dynamics. Achieves 95.8%+ on RoboTwin 2.0 under clean and randomized settings with 50× speedup via step reduction, compilation, and FP8 quantization. DIFFERENTIATION from CDR: MotuBrain is a training-time architectural approach for unified multimodal modeling; CDR is post-hoc test-time routing on a frozen mimic-video checkpoint requiring no backbone retraining. These are complementary — MotuBrain could serve as a future CDR base model if it supports variable-τ_v inference. Reviewers may mention MotuBrain as related work; distinguish on training-time architecture vs. test-time routing.

D3P (arXiv:2508.06804) adapts ACTION denoising steps via RL — complementary efficiency axis (same as VADF, different mechanism). X-WAM (arXiv:2604.26694) uses Asynchronous Noise Sampling from a fixed joint distribution — not per-observation adaptive. UWM (arXiv:2504.02792) uses independent modality timesteps from fixed schedule. Being-H0.7 (arXiv:2605.00078) avoids pixel decoding via distillation. S-VAM (arXiv:2603.16195) distills multi-step to one-step; requires retraining. 'When to Trust Imagination' (arXiv:2605.06222) introduces a per-action-chunk adaptive replanning trigger: after each partial action execution, a learned threshold (τ=0.5) decides whether to continue executing the current plan or replan based on prediction reliability — orthogonal to CDR's per-observation τ_v routing.

No existing VAM paper: (a) uses GT-action-referenced τ_v labeling; (b) provides the first empirical characterization of which 3D manipulation phases need τ_v < 1 below the confirmed best fixed-global τ_v=1 in WAMs trained with logit-normal variable-τ_v augmentation; or (c) trains a zero-shot per-task/per-observation τ_v predictor that generalizes across tasks without offline rollouts.",
  "approach": "CDR has four sequenced phases relative to a deployed mimic-video checkpoint (no backbone retraining required):

**Phase 0 — Sanity Check + Preliminary Zero-Shot Validation (1–3 H100-hours, PREREQUISITE, run immediately):**
Take 5 LIBERO tasks spanning types (2 precision grasp/insert, 2 pick-and-place, 1 long-horizon). Run 3 demonstration trajectories each (~1,500 frames total). Sweep τ_v ∈ {1.0, 0.9, ..., 0.1} using the frozen mimic-video action decoder. Compute τ_v*(f) = argmin_{τ_v ∈ {1.0,...,0.1}} ||a_{τ_v}(f) − a_GT(f)||₂ for each frame f (GT action from demo teleop). Annotate frames by manipulation phase using end-effector distance to target + gripper state.

[NEW] Preliminary zero-shot validation (run within Phase 0, ~1 additional H100-hour): Using CLIP image and frozen mimic-video language embeddings for the 5 tasks, train a task-level τ_v MLP on task-mean τ_v* from tasks 1–4. Evaluate zero-shot prediction on task 5. This 4→1 leave-one-out check validates whether task embedding space contains τ_v-predictive signal before committing the zero-shot LIBERO→SIMPLER-Bridge claim as a primary CoRL contribution. If prediction error on the held-out task is <20% of task 5's τ_v* value: preliminary evidence supports zero-shot generalization — proceed with zero-shot claim. If >20%: plan to include few-shot SIMPLER-Bridge adaptation (3 tasks) as fallback framing for Phase 3. Full 80/20 LIBERO held-out validation runs in Phase 2.

Decision gate (by May 12):
- If <10% of frames have τ_v* < 0.9 (nearly all frames prefer τ_v=1 for action quality): per-observation variation is minimal. Pivot paper framing to 'τ_v=1 universality study + automated zero-shot per-task routing' — do NOT commit to full Phase 1 scope. Reframe contribution as empirical validation + deployment automation.
- If ≥20% of frames have τ_v* < 0.9 AND these cluster in grasp/insert phases: full selective activation story is empirically supported. Proceed to Phase 1.
- Intermediate (10–20%): assess within-episode vs. across-task variance before proceeding.

**Phase 1 — 3D Video Necessity Study (~40–60 H100-hours): The Primary Empirical Contribution**
For each frame f in LIBERO-100 (100 tasks × 50 demos × ~100 steps ≈ 500K frames), compute:

  τ_v*(f) = argmin_{τ_v ∈ {1.0, 0.9, ..., 0.1}} ||a_{τ_v}(f) − a_GT(f)||₂

where a_GT(f) is the ground-truth demonstration action at frame f (available from LIBERO-100 teleop data) and a_{τ_v}(f) is the mimic-video action decoder output with τ_v-noised video input. The sweep range {1.0,...,0.1} excludes τ_v=0 entirely (confirmed worse than intermediate τ_v in mimic-video). NOTE: τ_v=1 is the expected modal value for τ_v*(f) given mimic-video's main-text finding; Phase 1 asks how many frames deviate from τ_v*=1.0, and whether deviations cluster in specific manipulation phases. The mimic-video per-task breakdown (Table I: Stack Blocks +16.7pp, Carrot on Plate +16.7pp, Spoon on Towel +4.2pp, Eggplant +0pp from per-task tuning) provides task-level priors: precision manipulation tasks (Stack Blocks, Carrot on Plate) are expected to show stronger clustering of τ_v*(f) < 0.9 than already-saturated tasks (Eggplant in Basket). Phase 1 confirms whether this task-level heterogeneity extends to within-task phase-level variation.

Annotate frames with manipulation phases: approach (end-effector distance > 5cm to target), pre-grasp (distance 1–5cm, gripper open), grasp (gripper closing event), transport (gripper closed, object moving), place (object near target, gripper opening). Derive from proprioceptive state; no additional network required.

Report: (a) Distribution of τ_v* — specifically fraction of frames where τ_v*=1.0 (consistent with mimic-video main text) vs. τ_v* < 0.9 (deviations from fixed-global optimal); (b) Mean τ_v* by manipulation phase — do grasp/insert phases show significantly lower τ_v* than approach/transport, characterizing for the FIRST TIME which 3D manipulation phases need video denoising below the τ_v=1 fixed-global default?; (c) Within-episode τ_v* variance vs. across-task τ_v* variance — which dominates?; (d) Whether LingBot-VA's fixed s≈0.6 corresponds to over-denoising for approach frames.

[SCOPE NOTE]: This characterization applies to WAM architectures trained with logit-normal variable-τ_v augmentation; architectures that do not expose τ_v as a continuous test-time parameter (e.g., Fast-WAM, which removes the video backbone at test time entirely) are architecturally incompatible with CDR's per-observation routing. The paper explicitly states this scope in the introduction: 'CDR's empirical findings characterize WAMs under logit-normal variable-τ_v training; this scope does not extend to architectures that eliminate τ_v as a test-time degree of freedom via retraining.'

[Distribution shift mitigation]: Include suboptimal rollout states to reduce demo-vs-rollout gap. Specifically: run the mimic-video policy (τ_v=1) 3× per task on LIBERO-100, collect frames from failed/recovery trajectories (partial grasps, dropped objects, recovery approaches). Add these to the labeling dataset (~50% of total labeled frames from non-expert trajectories). This gives the router diverse training states including recovery behaviors seen during closed-loop evaluation.

Compute: ~750K frames × 10 τ_v levels = ~7.5M backbone forward passes. With batch=64 on Cosmos-Predict2 (2B DiT), ~40–60 H100-hours.

**Phase 2 — Router Training + Zero-Shot Hold-Out Validation (~6 H100-hours):**
4-class router: {τ_v=1.0 (no activation), τ_v∈[0.7,0.9] (light activation), τ_v∈[0.4,0.6] (medium activation), τ_v∈[0.1,0.3] (heavy activation)}. Labels from Phase 1 mapped to nearest class bin. Architecture: two-layer MLP (512-dim CLIP image embedding + 512-dim frozen mimic-video language embedding → 256-dim hidden ReLU → 4-class softmax). Loss: CE(τ̂, τ_v*_class) + λ·E[τ̂_consumed].

Conservative routing (addressing distribution shift): if max softmax probability < θ, predict τ_v=1.0 regardless of argmax — since τ_v=1 is the confirmed best fixed-global default, falling back to it on uncertain (OOD) states avoids unnecessary compute overhead while maintaining the quality floor. Sweep λ ∈ {0.01, 0.1} and θ ∈ {0.5, 0.7} to trace the accuracy-efficiency frontier (reduced from full grid to fit within compute budget).

Task-level CDR variant: also train on task-mean τ_v* (average τ_v* across all frames in a task) to enable the per-task routing baseline (d) and test zero-shot generalization on SIMPLER-Bridge.

[NEW] 80/20 LIBERO held-out validation (REQUIRED before finalizing zero-shot CoRL claim): Split LIBERO-100 into 80 training / 20 held-out tasks (stratified by task type). Train task-level τ_v MLP on 80 tasks' task-mean τ_v*. Test zero-shot on 20 held-out tasks: measure τ_v* recovery = (gain from predicted τ_v vs. τ_v=1) / (oracle gain from true τ_v* vs. τ_v=1).

Zero-shot claim gate:
- If ≥80% τ_v* recovery on 20 held-out LIBERO tasks → zero-shot LIBERO→SIMPLER-Bridge claim is empirically credible. Keep as primary CoRL claim: 'per-task CDR recovers ≥80% of +9.4pp zero-shot on SIMPLER-Bridge.'
- If <80% recovery on held-out LIBERO tasks → reframe to 'per-task routing with few-shot adaptation on 3 SIMPLER-Bridge tasks': train task-level MLP on the 3 SIMPLER-Bridge tasks with most available rollouts, test on remaining SIMPLER-Bridge tasks. This is still a deployment contribution (reduces 10-rollout per-task sweep to 3-task fine-tuning) but scoped more conservatively.

**Phase 3 — Evaluation (~50 H100-hours, primary benchmark: SIMPLER-Bridge):**

[ELEVATED ANCHOR CLAIM] Formal Pre-Registered Prediction: The primary competitive framing is CDR vs. τ_v=1 fixed-global baseline. We formally pre-register two predictions before running Phase 3 experiments:
  (P1) Fixed intermediate τ_v baselines (b: τ_v=0.5; c: τ_v=0.7 and τ_v=0.9) will UNDERPERFORM baseline (a) τ_v=1 on SIMPLER-Bridge. This prediction is strongly supported by mimic-video's main text ('the best autonomous policy performance in our SIMPLER experiments is achieved at the highest noise level τ_v=1'). The pre-registration converts a potential 'cherry-picked baselines' concern into a published empirical confirmation of mimic-video's finding.
